question: Community Development Programme was under the __________ Five-Year Plan in India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**First**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Community Development Programme was launched during the **First Five-Year Plan** in India (1951-1956).
 
• It aimed at providing an integrated approach to the improvement of agriculture, irrigation, and communication in rural areas.
 
• The programme started on October 2, 1952, with a focus on the holistic development of rural areas through people's participation.
 
• It was a pioneering effort towards rural development in India, laying the foundation for subsequent development initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956)**

 
 
• It was focused on agricultural development, with the highest priority given to irrigation and energy production.
 
• The plan aimed at reducing the dependency on food grain imports by increasing domestic agricultural production.
 
• It was based on the Harrod-Domar model, emphasizing the growth rate of the economy.
 
 
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)**
 
 
• This plan focused on industrialization, particularly on the development of heavy industries and the public sector.
 
• It aimed to build a self-reliant economy through rapid industrial growth.
 
• Planned on the Mahalanobis model, which emphasized the importance of capital goods industries.
 
 
 
• **Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966)**
 
 
• It aimed at making India a self-reliant and self-generating economy.
 
• Focused on the agriculture sector to address food security and emphasized the importance of education.
 
• The plan faced challenges like the Indo-China war (1962), Indo-Pak war (1965), and severe droughts.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974)**
 
 
• It focused on "Growth with Stability" and emphasized the need for a stable economy.
 
• Introduced the concept of Minimum Needs Programme (MNP) for the poor.
 
• It aimed at reducing the concentration of wealth and economic power.
